parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Gibberellin is a plant growth regulator involved in barley seed germination. Production of gibberellin is stimulated by the uptake of water.

State the location of gibberellin synthesis in a barley seed during germination.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Barley seeds germinate when placed on blotting (absorbent) paper soaked in water.

The germination of barley seeds placed on blotting paper soaked in solutions of different water potential was investigated.

The success of germination was measured as a germination index for:
• barley seeds placed on blotting paper soaked in water
• barley seeds placed on blotting paper soaked in 5 solutions of different water potential.

The results are shown in Fig. 5.1.

The higher the germination index value, the more successful the germination of the barley seeds.

{{figure:figure_5_1.webp}}

Fig. 5.1

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 5.1, describe the relationship between the germination index of barley seeds and water potential.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest explanations for the relationship shown in Fig. 5.1.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
During barley seed germination, gibberellin stimulates the synthesis of enzymes.

State the name of one of these enzymes **and** the precise location of its synthesis.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
Some plants are grown commercially for their flowers. Many of these plants are varieties that have short stems.

Two factors that affect the height of stems are:
• gibberellin
• the $Le$/$le$ gene.

The $Le$/$le$ gene has two alleles, $Le$ and $le$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Suggest an advantage of growing a short-stemmed variety of a flowering plant.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how the $Le$/$le$ gene and gibberellin are involved in affecting the height of plant stems.
